learn.b: こんにちは (konnichiwa) means hello. おはよう (ohayou) is good morning, and こんばんは (konbanwa) is good evening. Use them at different times of the day.
ありがとう (arigatou) means thank you. すみません (sumimasen) means excuse me or sorry. さようなら (sayounara) means goodbye.
Say はじめまして (hajimemashite) when you meet someone. Then say わたしは ○○ です (watashi wa ○○ desu), which means I am ○○.

qs.q: What does こんにちは (konnichiwa) mean?
qs.why: こんにちは (konnichiwa) is the standard daytime hello.

qs.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Japanese?
qs.why: ありがとう (arigatou) means thank you.

qs.q: Which greeting do you use in the morning?
qs.why: おはよう (ohayou) means good morning.

qs.q: How do you say 'I am Ken' politely?
o: ケン を たべます (Ken o tabemasu)
ケン が すき (Ken ga suki)
ケン に いきます (Ken ni ikimasu)
わたしは ケン です (watashi wa Ken desu)
qs.why: わたしは ○○ です (watashi wa ○○ desu) is the pattern for I am ○○.

qs.q: さようなら (sayounara) means goodbye.
qs.why: さようなら (sayounara) is used to say goodbye.

qs.q: Match each Japanese greeting to its meaning
Put these greetings in order from morning to night

learn.b: いち (ichi) is 1, に (ni) is 2, さん (san) is 3, よん (yon) is 4, and ご (go) is 5. In writing they look like 一, 二, 三.
ろく (roku) is 6, なな (nana) is 7, はち (hachi) is 8, きゅう (kyuu) is 9, and じゅう (juu) is 10.
おかあさん (okaasan) is mother and おとうさん (otousan) is father. いもうと (imouto) is younger sister. かぞく (kazoku) means family.

qs.q: What number is さん (san)?
How do you say 'five' in Japanese?
What does おかあさん (okaasan) mean?
How do you say 'father' politely?
はち (hachi) means seven.
qs.why: はち (hachi) means eight. Seven is なな (nana).

qs.q: Match each number word to its number
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: ごはん (gohan) is rice or a meal. さかな (sakana) is fish and にく (niku) is meat. りんご (ringo) is apple and パン (pan) is bread.
みず (mizu) is water and おちゃ (ocha) is tea. たべます (tabemasu) means eat and のみます (nomimasu) means drink.
おいしい (oishii) means delicious. すき (suki) means like. ください (kudasai) means please give me.

qs.q: What does みず (mizu) mean?
How do you say 'I drink tea'?
o: おちゃを たべます (ocha o tabemasu)
おちゃを のみます (ocha o nomimasu)
みずを たべます (mizu o tabemasu)
ごはんを のみます (gohan o nomimasu)
qs.why: のみます (nomimasu) is the verb for drinking, and おちゃ (ocha) is tea.

qs.q: What does おいしい (oishii) mean?
Which food is りんご (ringo)?
パン (pan) means bread.
qs.why: パン (pan) is bread, borrowed from Portuguese.

qs.q: Match each food word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I eat fish every day

learn.b: です (desu) is like am, is, or are. Add か (ka) at the end to make a question. がっこうですか (gakkou desu ka) means Is it school?
Polite verbs end in ます (masu). いきます (ikimasu) means go, きます (kimasu) means come, and みます (mimasu) means see or watch.
Change ます (masu) to ません (masen) for no. たべません (tabemasen) means do not eat. Use います (imasu) for living things and あります (arimasu) for objects.

qs.q: What does か (ka) at the end of a sentence do?
qs.why: か (ka) turns a sentence into a question.

qs.q: What does いきます (ikimasu) mean?
What is the negative of たべます (tabemasu)?
qs.why: Replace ます (masu) with ません (masen) to make a verb negative.

qs.q: Which sentence means 'There is a cat'?
o: ねこが あります (neko ga arimasu)
ねこを たべます (neko o tabemasu)
ねこが いきます (neko ga ikimasu)
ねこが います (neko ga imasu)
qs.why: Animals are living things, so they use います (imasu).

qs.q: がっこう (gakkou) means school.
qs.why: がっこう (gakkou) is the word for school.

qs.q: Match each verb to its meaning
Put the words in order: I go to school every day

learn.b: Change ます (masu) to ました (mashita) for the past. たべます (tabemasu) becomes たべました (tabemashita), which means ate.
Use ませんでした (masen deshita) for did not. いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita) means did not go. The past of です (desu) is でした (deshita).
きのう (kinou) means yesterday. けさ (kesa) means this morning. These words often come near the start of the sentence.

qs.q: What does たべました (tabemashita) mean?
qs.why: ました (mashita) shows past tense, so it means ate.

qs.q: What does きのう (kinou) mean?
How do you say 'I did not go'?
o: いきませんでした (ikimasen deshita)
qs.why: ませんでした (masen deshita) is the polite past negative.

qs.q: What is the past of です (desu)?
qs.why: でした (deshita) is the past form of です (desu).

qs.q: ませんでした (masen deshita) is the polite past negative ending.
qs.why: It means did not, for example たべませんでした (tabemasen deshita) means did not eat.

qs.q: Match each present verb to its past form
Put the words in order: I watched a movie yesterday

learn.b: どこ (doko) means where. えきは どこですか (eki wa doko desu ka) means Where is the station? The word えき (eki) means station.
みぎ (migi) is right and ひだり (hidari) is left. まっすぐ (massugu) is straight. まがります (magarimasu) means turn.
びょういん (byouin) is hospital and ぎんこう (ginkou) is bank. ちかい (chikai) means near and とおい (tooi) means far.

qs.q: What does えきは どこですか (eki wa doko desu ka) mean?
qs.why: どこ (doko) means where, and えき (eki) means station.

qs.q: What does みぎ (migi) mean?
What does まっすぐ (massugu) mean?
qs.why: まっすぐ (massugu) means straight ahead.

qs.q: How do you say 'Please turn left'?
o: みぎに まがってください (migi ni magatte kudasai)
まっすぐ たべてください (massugu tabete kudasai)
ひだりに まがってください (hidari ni magatte kudasai)
ひだりは どこですか (hidari wa doko desu ka)
qs.why: ひだり (hidari) is left, and まがってください (magatte kudasai) means please turn.

qs.q: とおい (tooi) means near.
qs.why: とおい (tooi) means far. Near is ちかい (chikai).

qs.q: Match each place to its meaning
Put the words in order: Excuse me, where is the bank?

learn.b: でんしゃ (densha) is train and ひこうき (hikouki) is airplane. きっぷ (kippu) is ticket. りょこう (ryokou) means trip.
いくらですか (ikura desu ka) means How much is it? たかい (takai) means expensive or high. やすい (yasui) means cheap.
Use ○○が ほしいです (○○ ga hoshii desu) for I want ○○. きっぷが ほしいです (kippu ga hoshii desu) means I want a ticket.

qs.q: What does いくらですか (ikura desu ka) mean?
What does でんしゃ (densha) mean?
What does たかい (takai) mean when talking about a price?
qs.why: たかい (takai) means high or expensive.

qs.q: How do you say 'I want a ticket'?
o: きっぷを みます (kippu o mimasu)
きっぷは どこですか (kippu wa doko desu ka)
きっぷが たかい (kippu ga takai)
きっぷが ほしいです (kippu ga hoshii desu)
qs.why: ほしいです (hoshii desu) means want.

qs.q: やすい (yasui) means expensive.
Match each travel word to its meaning
Put the words in order: How much is this ticket?

learn.b: おもしろい (omoshiroi) means interesting or fun. つまらない (tsumaranai) means boring. かんたん (kantan) means easy and むずかしい (muzukashii) means difficult.
Add と おもいます (to omoimasu) to say I think. おもしろいと おもいます (omoshiroi to omoimasu) means I think it is fun.
どうして (doushite) means why. から (kara) means because and goes after the reason. けど (kedo) means but.

qs.q: How do you say 'I think it is fun'?
o: おもしろいと おもいます (omoshiroi to omoimasu)
おもしろいを たべます (omoshiroi o tabemasu)
つまらないですか (tsumaranai desu ka)
おもしろいに いきます (omoshiroi ni ikimasu)
qs.why: と おもいます (to omoimasu) means I think.

qs.q: What does むずかしい (muzukashii) mean?
What does どうして (doushite) mean?
What does から (kara) mean after a reason?
qs.why: から (kara) after a clause means because.

qs.q: きらい (kirai) means like.
qs.why: きらい (kirai) means dislike. Like is すき (suki).

qs.q: Match each describing word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I think Japanese is interesting

learn.b: Mandarin has four tones. The 1st is high and level (mā), the 2nd rises (má), the 3rd dips (mǎ), and the 4th falls (mà). The tone changes the meaning.
你好 (nǐ hǎo) means hello. 谢谢 (xièxie) means thank you and 不客气 (bú kèqi) means you're welcome. 再见 (zàijiàn) means goodbye.
Say 我叫 (wǒ jiào) and then your name. 我叫李 (wǒ jiào Lǐ) means My name is Li. 对不起 (duìbuqǐ) means sorry.

qs.q: What does 你好 (nǐ hǎo) mean?
qs.why: 你好 (nǐ hǎo) is the basic hello.

qs.q: How do you say 'thank you' in Mandarin?
What does 再见 (zàijiàn) mean?
How do you say 'My name is Li'?
qs.why: 我叫 (wǒ jiào) means my name is.

qs.q: 对不起 (duìbuqǐ) means sorry.
qs.why: 对不起 (duìbuqǐ) is used to apologize.

qs.q: Match each phrase to its meaning
Put the four Mandarin tones in order, 1st to 4th

learn.b: 一 (yī) is 1, 二 (èr) is 2, 三 (sān) is 3, 四 (sì) is 4, and 五 (wǔ) is 5. The first three are simple lines.
六 (liù) is 6, 七 (qī) is 7, 八 (bā) is 8, 九 (jiǔ) is 9, and 十 (shí) is 10.
妈妈 (māma) is mom and 爸爸 (bàba) is dad. 哥哥 (gēge) is older brother and 姐姐 (jiějie) is older sister. 弟弟 (dìdi) and 妹妹 (mèimei) are younger brother and younger sister.

qs.q: What number is 三 (sān)?
qs.why: 三 (sān) has three lines and means 3.

qs.q: How do you say 'eight' in Mandarin?
What does 妈妈 (māma) mean?
How do you say 'older sister'?
十 (shí) means ten.
Match each family word to its meaning
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: 吃 (chī) means to eat and 喝 (hē) means to drink. 我吃米饭 (wǒ chī mǐfàn) means I eat rice. 我喝水 (wǒ hē shuǐ) means I drink water.
米饭 (mǐfàn) is rice and 面条 (miàntiáo) is noodles. 鱼 (yú) is fish and 苹果 (píngguǒ) is apple. 水 (shuǐ) is water and 茶 (chá) is tea.
我想 (wǒ xiǎng) means I would like. 好吃 (hǎochī) means delicious. 我要 (wǒ yào) means I want.

qs.q: What does 水 (shuǐ) mean?
How do you say 'I drink tea'?
qs.why: 喝 (hē) is used for drinking, and 茶 (chá) is tea.

qs.q: What does 好吃 (hǎochī) mean?
qs.why: 好吃 (hǎochī) means tasty or delicious.

qs.q: Which food is 苹果 (píngguǒ)?
吃 (chī) means to drink.
qs.why: 吃 (chī) means to eat. To drink is 喝 (hē).

qs.q: Match each food word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I eat rice every day

learn.b: 是 (shì) means to be. 我是学生 (wǒ shì xuéshēng) means I am a student. 有 (yǒu) means to have. 我有一只猫 (wǒ yǒu yì zhī māo) means I have a cat.
Use 不 (bù) before most verbs. 不是 (bú shì) means is not. Use 没有 (méiyǒu) for do not have.
Add 吗 (ma) at the end to make a yes or no question. 去 (qù) means go and 来 (lái) means come. 学校 (xuéxiào) means school.

qs.q: What does 吗 (ma) do at the end of a sentence?
qs.why: 吗 (ma) turns a statement into a yes or no question.

qs.q: How do you say 'I have a cat'?
o: 我有一只猫 (wǒ yǒu yì zhī māo)
我是一只猫 (wǒ shì yì zhī māo)
我去一只猫 (wǒ qù yì zhī māo)

qs.q: What does 去 (qù) mean?
What is the negative of 是 (shì)?
qs.why: 不是 (bú shì) means is not or am not.

qs.q: 没有 (méiyǒu) means 'do not have'.
qs.why: 没有 (méiyǒu) is the negative of 有 (yǒu).

qs.q: Match each verb to its meaning
Put the words in order: I go to school every day

learn.b: Put 了 (le) after a verb to show an action is done. 我吃了 (wǒ chī le) means I ate. 昨天 (zuótiān) means yesterday.
Put 过 (guo) after a verb to say you have done it before. 我去过中国 (wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó) means I have been to China.
Use 没 (méi) to say you did not do something. 我没吃饭 (wǒ méi chī fàn) means I did not eat. Do not add 了 (le) after it.

qs.q: What does 昨天 (zuótiān) mean?
How do you say 'I ate'?
o: 我不吃吗 (wǒ bù chī ma)
我没吃了 (wǒ méi chī le)
qs.why: 了 (le) after the verb shows the action is complete.

qs.q: How do you say 'I have been to China'?
o: 我去了中国吗 (wǒ qù le Zhōngguó ma)
我去过中国 (wǒ qù guo Zhōngguó)

qs.q: How do you say 'I did not go'?
o: 我不去了 (wǒ bù qù le)
qs.why: 没 (méi) is used to negate past actions.

qs.q: 了 (le) often shows that an action is completed.
qs.why: 了 (le) marks a completed action, as in 我吃了 (wǒ chī le).

qs.q: Match each time word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I watched a movie yesterday

learn.b: 哪儿 (nǎr) means where. 银行在哪儿 (yínháng zài nǎr) means Where is the bank? 在 (zài) means at or is located at.
左 (zuǒ) is left and 右 (yòu) is right. 一直走 (yìzhí zǒu) means go straight. 转 (zhuǎn) means turn.
医院 (yīyuàn) is hospital and 火车站 (huǒchēzhàn) is train station. 近 (jìn) means near and 远 (yuǎn) means far. 附近 (fùjìn) means nearby.

qs.q: What does 银行在哪儿 (yínháng zài nǎr) mean?
What does 右 (yòu) mean?
What does 一直走 (yìzhí zǒu) mean?
qs.why: 一直 (yìzhí) means straight and 走 (zǒu) means walk or go.

qs.q: How do you say 'turn left'?
qs.why: 左 (zuǒ) is left and 转 (zhuǎn) is turn.

qs.q: 远 (yuǎn) means near.
qs.why: 远 (yuǎn) means far. Near is 近 (jìn).

qs.q: Match each place to its meaning
Put the words in order: Excuse me, where is the hospital?

learn.b: 多少钱 (duōshao qián) means How much? 贵 (guì) means expensive and 便宜 (piányi) means cheap.
机票 (jīpiào) is plane ticket and 酒店 (jiǔdiàn) is hotel. 护照 (hùzhào) is passport and 旅行 (lǚxíng) means travel. 地铁 (dìtiě) is subway.
买 (mǎi) means buy. 我想买机票 (wǒ xiǎng mǎi jīpiào) means I want to buy a plane ticket. 坐 (zuò) means to take a vehicle.

qs.q: What does 多少钱 (duōshao qián) mean?
qs.why: 多少钱 (duōshao qián) asks the price.

qs.q: What does 贵 (guì) mean?
What is 护照 (hùzhào)?
How do you say 'I want to buy a ticket'?
o: 我想买机票 (wǒ xiǎng mǎi jīpiào)
我想吃机票 (wǒ xiǎng chī jīpiào)
我不是机票 (wǒ bú shì jīpiào)
我去过机票 (wǒ qù guo jīpiào)
qs.why: 想 (xiǎng) means want and 买 (mǎi) means buy.

qs.q: 便宜 (piányi) means expensive.
Match each travel word to its meaning
Put the words in order: How much is this ticket?

learn.b: 觉得 (juéde) means to think or feel. 我觉得很有意思 (wǒ juéde hěn yǒu yìsi) means I think it is very interesting. 喜欢 (xǐhuan) means like.
因为 (yīnwèi) means because and 所以 (suǒyǐ) means so. 但是 (dànshì) means but.
Use 比 (bǐ) to compare. 他比我高 (tā bǐ wǒ gāo) means He is taller than me. 更 (gèng) means even more.

qs.q: How do you say 'I think it is very interesting'?
o: 我不是有意思 (wǒ bú shì yǒu yìsi)
我去很有意思 (wǒ qù hěn yǒu yìsi)
我吃很有意思 (wǒ chī hěn yǒu yìsi)
我觉得很有意思 (wǒ juéde hěn yǒu yìsi)

qs.q: What does 因为 (yīnwèi) mean?
How do you say 'He is taller than me'?
o: 他比我高 (tā bǐ wǒ gāo)
他和我高 (tā hé wǒ gāo)
他不是高 (tā bú shì gāo)
他去我高 (tā qù wǒ gāo)

qs.q: What does 难 (nán) mean?
qs.why: 难 (nán) means difficult. Easy is 容易 (róngyì).

qs.q: 但是 (dànshì) means 'because'.
Match each connecting word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I think Chinese is interesting

learn.b: 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo) means hello. 감사합니다 (gamsahamnida) means thank you. 죄송합니다 (joesonghamnida) means I am sorry.
네 (ne) means yes and 아니요 (aniyo) means no. Say 안녕히 가세요 (annyeonghi gaseyo) to someone who is leaving. Say 안녕히 계세요 (annyeonghi gyeseyo) to someone who is staying.
Say 저는 민입니다 (jeoneun Min-imnida) for I am Min. 만나서 반갑습니다 (mannaseo bangapseumnida) means nice to meet you.

qs.q: What does 안녕하세요 (annyeonghaseyo) mean?
How do you say 'thank you' in Korean?
Which word means 'yes'?
How do you say 'I am Min' politely?
qs.why: 저는 (jeoneun) means I, and 입니다 (imnida) means am.

qs.q: 아니요 (aniyo) means yes.
Match each phrase to its meaning
Put this short conversation in order

learn.b: These numbers are used for dates, money, and phone numbers. 일 (il) is 1, 이 (i) is 2, 삼 (sam) is 3, 사 (sa) is 4, 오 (o) is 5. 육 (yuk) is 6, 칠 (chil) is 7, 팔 (pal) is 8, 구 (gu) is 9, 십 (sip) is 10.
These numbers are used for counting things and for age. 하나 (hana) is 1, 둘 (dul) is 2, and 셋 (set) is 3.
엄마 (eomma) is mom and 아빠 (appa) is dad. 동생 (dongsaeng) is a younger brother or sister. 가족 (gajok) means family.

qs.q: What number is 삼 (sam)?
qs.why: 삼 (sam) is 3 in the Sino-Korean system.

qs.q: How do you say 'ten' in Sino-Korean?
What does 엄마 (eomma) mean?
What does 가족 (gajok) mean?
하나 (hana) means one.
qs.why: 하나 (hana) is the native Korean word for 1.

qs.q: Match each family word to its meaning
Put these numbers in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: 밥 (bap) means cooked rice or a meal. 김치 (gimchi) is kimchi and 고기 (gogi) is meat. 사과 (sagwa) is apple and 물 (mul) is water.
먹어요 (meogeoyo) means eat. 마셔요 (masyeoyo) means drink. 저는 밥을 먹어요 (jeoneun babeul meogeoyo) means I eat rice.
Say 물 주세요 (mul juseyo) for Please give me water. 맛있어요 (masisseoyo) means delicious. 좋아해요 (joahaeyo) means like.

qs.q: What does 물 (mul) mean?
How do you say 'Please give me water'?
What does 맛있어요 (masisseoyo) mean?
Which food is 사과 (sagwa)?
밥 (bap) can mean cooked rice or a meal.
qs.why: 밥 (bap) means rice, and also a meal in general.

qs.q: Match each food word to its meaning
Put the words in order: I eat rice every day

learn.b: 이에요 (ieyo) or 예요 (yeyo) means is or am. 학생이에요 (haksaengieyo) means I am a student. Use 이에요 after a consonant and 예요 after a vowel.
있어요 (isseoyo) means have or there is. 없어요 (eopseoyo) means do not have or there is not.
가요 (gayo) means go and 와요 (wayo) means come. Put 안 (an) before a verb to make it negative. 안 먹어요 (an meogeoyo) means do not eat.

qs.q: What does 가요 (gayo) mean?
What does 없어요 (eopseoyo) mean?
o: I do not have, there is not
qs.why: 없어요 (eopseoyo) is the opposite of 있어요 (isseoyo).

qs.q: What does 안 먹어요 (an meogeoyo) mean?
qs.why: 안 (an) before a verb makes it negative.

qs.q: What does 학교 (hakgyo) mean?
있어요 (isseoyo) can mean 'there is' or 'I have'.
qs.why: 있어요 (isseoyo) shows that something exists or is owned.

qs.q: Match each verb to its meaning
Put the words in order: I go to school every day

learn.b: Add 았어요 or 었어요 (asseoyo or eosseoyo) to the verb stem. 먹다 (meokda) becomes 먹었어요 (meogeosseoyo), which means ate. 가다 (gada) becomes 갔어요 (gasseoyo), which means went.
Put 안 (an) before the past verb. 안 갔어요 (an gasseoyo) means did not go.
어제 (eoje) means yesterday and 오늘 (oneul) means today. 내일 (naeil) means tomorrow. 지난주 (jinanju) means last week.

qs.q: What does 어제 (eoje) mean?
How do you say 'I ate'?
What does 갔어요 (gasseoyo) mean?
qs.why: 갔어요 (gasseoyo) is the past of 가다 (gada), to go.

qs.q: How do you say 'I did not go'?

learn.b: For regular verbs, add ed to talk about the past. Play becomes played and walk becomes walked. We often use words like yesterday and last week.
Some common verbs change form. Go becomes went, eat becomes ate, see becomes saw, and have becomes had. You need to learn these.
Use didn't plus the base verb. I didn't go to school. Do not add ed after didn't.

learn.b: Say Turn left or Turn right. Say Go straight to keep walking forward. Say Stop at the corner when you must stop.
Next to means beside. Opposite means on the other side. Between means in the middle of two things. Near means close and far means a long way away.
Start with Excuse me. Then ask Where is the bank? or How do I get to the station? These questions are polite and clear.

qs.q: Which word is the opposite of 'left'?
qs.why: Left and right are opposite directions.

qs.q: Which question asks for directions politely?
o: Excuse me, how do I get to the station?
qs.why: It uses Excuse me and a full question.

qs.why: Go straight means keep going forward.

qs.q: 'Far' means a short distance away.
qs.why: Far means a long distance away. Near means a short distance.

learn.b: A passport lets you travel to other countries. A ticket lets you take a train or plane. An airport is where planes land. A hotel is where you sleep on a trip.
Ask How much is this? to learn the price. Expensive means it costs a lot. Cheap means it costs little. A receipt is paper that shows what you paid.
Say I'd like to buy this, please. Say I'd like to book a room for two nights. You can also ask Can I pay by card?

qs.q: Which word means 'costs a lot of money'?
qs.why: Expensive means it costs a lot.

qs.q: You show this at the airport to travel to another country.
qs.why: A passport proves who you are when you travel abroad.

qs.q: How do you ask the price of something?
qs.why: How much is this? asks about the price.

qs.q: Where do you sleep when you travel?
qs.why: A hotel is a place to sleep on a trip.

qs.q: 'Cheap' means something costs a lot.
qs.why: Cheap means it costs very little.

learn.b: Start with I think, I believe, or In my opinion. Say I agree if you think the same. Say I disagree if you think differently.
Because gives a reason. But shows a contrast. So shows a result. For example: I was tired, so I went to bed.
Use am, is, or are going to plus a verb for a plan: I am going to travel next year. Use more before long adjectives: more interesting. Use er for short ones: bigger.

qs.q: What does 'I agree' mean?
qs.why: To agree is to think the same as someone.

qs.q: Choose the correct word: I ___ going to travel next year.
qs.why: Use am with I in the going to future.

qs.why: Long adjectives use more in the comparative.
